messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 95th pct streaming latency for hosted/text-stream endpoint in us-west-2. Impact: user-visible streaming stalls. Aggregated error rate + latency spike recorded at 23:44:36 UTC. Paging oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: Acknowledged. Looking at logs now. Can someone confirm customer-facing impact? Which routes are affected?
alex: I'm seeing a spike on /v1/stream TEXT route for model 'redwood-13b-quant'. Tail logs show lots of repeated 502s from model host pool.
maria: Confirmed, we've got 3 customers reporting stalled streams, one using live chat. Latency goes from 120ms to >10s and then a stall.
sam: Reproducer attached: small local curl reproduces stalls when sequence length ~1500 tokens.
eng-runtime: Pinging serving teams. I see kernel timeouts on gpu-node-17 around 23:44:28. Suspect KV cache eviction thrash after a config change earlier today.
alex: Reminder: we rolled batching/autoscale tweak at 21:10 (enable aggressive batching) for cost efficiency. That could be related.
product-ops: Noted. Customer impacts logged in INC-840. Prioritize live mitigation.
eng-runtime: Collecting stack traces and dmesg from gpu-node-17. Also dumping model server logs (excerpt):
```
[23:44:25] SERVE ERR: kv_cache_miss_count=12234
[23:44:26] WARNING: kernel_launch_timeout after 3000ms
[23:44:27] SERVE ERR: stream_write_timeout
[23:44:28] Traceback: RuntimeError: device-side assert
```
nora-support: Pushed a note to the affected customers: "We're investigating streaming stalls. We'll update in ~15m."
oncall-sre: Hypothesis list (initial): 1) batching change causing long tail due to oversized batches + kernel timeouts 2) kv-cache eviction bug after autoscale 3) model variant change/quantization mismatch 4) GPU driver/kernel regression 5) network flapping between routing layer and host pool. Which to test first?
alex: Prioritize (1) batching + (2) kv-cache. Easiest quick mitigation is to revert batching config to previous thresholds. I can flip that, need a quick thumbs.
maria: +1 revert batching. That should reduce batch sizes and avoid kernel overload.
eng-runtime: I'll start a canary rollback of batching config to 'batch_limit: 64, max_delay_ms: 20' on one pool. Command:
```bash
redwoodctl patch pool gpu-pool-west --set batching.batch_limit=64 --set batching.max_delay_ms=20 --namespace=prod-us-west-2
```
eng-runtime: Deploying canary to 10% pool now. Monitoring metrics.
incident-bot: :gear: deploy-bot started canary: deploy/rollback-batching-1862109876 to pool gpu-pool-west (10%) by eng-runtime.
alex: While canary runs, propose running a KV-cache diagnostic and toggling evictions to 'lru-strict' for affected hosts. That requires node restart? eng-runtime?
eng-runtime: KV toggle doesn't require restart; can set runtime flag. I'll enable 'kv_cache.eviction_policy=lru-strict' on node gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-18 now. Command: `redwood-runtime set-flag --node gpu-node-17 --flag kv_cache.eviction_policy=lru-strict`
eng-runtime: Flag set on both nodes. Observing reduced miss rate.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: canary deploy (rollback-batching-1862109876) shows 80% reduction in 95th latency on canary hosts within 90s.
oncall-sre: Nice. Continue ramp. Alex, can you coordinate a full rollback if health stays good for 3m?
alex: Yes. I'll promote to 100% after 3m stable. Also request eng-runtime to collect a heap profile before full rollback.
eng-runtime: Collecting heap/profile: `redwoodctl logs gpu-node-17 --profile --since 5m > /tmp/profile-1862109876.pb`
maria: Support update to customers: "We've implemented a mitigation and are monitoring. We'll follow up with RCA and timeline." :thumbsup:
sam: Running a quick revert test locally by toggling batching config in staging. Reproducer now passes without stalls after lowering batch window.
eng-runtime: Full rollback to previous batching config promoted at 23:47:10. Queue size normalized. Metrics: 95th latency back to baseline within 30s.
incident-bot: :tada: Incident mitigation success: streaming latency reduced to normal. Status: mitigated. Please continue RCA in-thread.
oncall-sre: Assigning owners: Alex (rollback owner), eng-runtime (root cause diagnostics + logs), Sam (repro + test harness), Maria (customer comms + timeline), Product-ops (post-incident follow-up).
alex: Preliminary conclusion: aggressive batching config increased end-to-end kernel load for long sequences causing kernel launch timeouts and interacting poorly with kv-cache eviction policy under memory pressure.
eng-runtime: We found evidence of increased KV cache churn after batching change: cache miss spikes + device RTOS scheduling delays. Also flagged a kernel-driver warning that we'll escalate.
sam: Action items for next 24h:
- reproduce at scale in staging with sequence lengths ~1k-2k (owner: sam)
- add canary gating for batching changes (owner: alex)
- add kv-cache metric alerting and slow-path tracing (owner: eng-runtime)
- run kernel-driver compatibility matrix (owner: eng-runtime)
- customer postmortem draft (owner: maria)
product-ops: Add SLA spillover check and update runbook to include 'rollback batching' step.
nora-support: I'll schedule customer follow-ups for tomorrow morning.
oncall-sre: Handoff: I'm leaving the pager in 15m to oncall 'eve'. I'll drop a short summary in #oncall-handoff. Final note: Incident mitigated but RCA ongoing. Keep updates here. :coffee:
alex: Thanks all. Will attach full traces and flamegraphs to this thread in 1h.
eng-runtime: Uploading logs to /incidents/1862109876/artifacts.tar.gz (s3 link) and will post hash.
incident-bot: :page_with_curl: Incident ticket INC-840 updated: mitigation recorded, owners assigned, next steps added.
maria: Closing interim customer comms: "Mitigation applied, monitoring now. We'll share full RCA in ~24-48h."
